title: Continuous lifts along stalkwise isomorphisms are scheme morphisms
statement: Let f : X → Y and g : W → Y be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose every stalk map of f is an isomorphism. For every continuous map a : |W| → |X| with f ∘ a = |g|, there is a unique scheme morphism m : W → X whose underlying map is a and with f ∘ m = g.

source.place: More precise statement following Lemma 2.2.8, inverse-image structure sheaf and its mapping property.

proof.text: Transpose the structure-sheaf morphism of f along presheaf inverse image and sheafification. The inverse-image stalk comparison and the sheafification stalk comparison identify its stalks with those of f. Hence it is an isomorphism of sheaves.

proof.text: Transpose the structure-sheaf map of g along the same adjunction and compose with the inverse isomorphism. Adjunction gives the required sheaf map above a and proves uniqueness.

proof.text: On stalks the resulting map is the stalk map of g composed with the inverse of the stalk map of f. Both are local homomorphisms, so it defines a scheme morphism. The adjunction equality says its composite with f is g.
